title: K20 presents comprehensive exhibition dedicated to Expressionist painter Franz Marc
summary: The Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen is presenting the first comprehensive exhibition dedicated to the Expressionist and co-founder of Der Blaue Reiter, Franz Marc (1880–1916), and thus the first major solo exhibition of his work in a German museum in over twenty years. Vibrant colors, deeply moving themes, and world-famous animal images—what makes the art of Franz Marc (1880–1916) so fascinating to this day? The exhibition Franz Marc. The Quest for a Better World at K20 invites visitors to rediscover the life and work of this outstanding artist. Through January 24, 2027, visitors have the unique opportunity to experience masterpieces from all phases of Franz Marc’s career in one place. Thanks to the support of numerous national and international public and private lenders, over 120 paintings and works on paper have been brought together. title: Almine Rech Paris presents Leonora Carrington solo exhibition
summary: From September 8 to October 10, 2026, Almine Rech Paris is dedicating a solo exhibition to Leonora Carrington (1917–2011), a leading figure in international Surrealism and one of the most singular artists in the history of art. Bringing together paintings, sculptures, works on paper, and masks, the gallery invites visitors to rediscover a body of work whose visionary power continues to fascinate through its ability to create a dialogue between myth, magic, and metamorphosis. Spanning the 20th century and its upheavals, from the rise of fascism to exile, Carrington nevertheless defies any strictly biographical interpretation. Neither muse, nor disciple, nor mere

title: Ancient glass from Phoenician perfume vessels to Roman luxury wares takes center stage at Artemis auction
summary: A small bottle in the form of the goddess Tyche, an unusually well-preserved Hellenistic drinking cup and a jewel-like Roman “basket jar” are among the ancient glass works taking center stage in Artemis Fine Arts and Arte Primitivo’s September 16 auction , a sale that offers collectors an unusually broad look at how glassmaking changed across the Mediterranean world over nearly a millennium. The sale is the second half of a two-day collaboration between Artemis Fine Arts and Arte Primitivo. Following a September 15 session devoted to Pre-Columbian, Native American material and fossils, the September 16 auction turns to Egyptian, Greek, Roman and Near Eastern antiquities alongside African, tribal and Asian art. title: Lars Eidinger brings his visual anthropology into dialogue with postwar art at Kunsthalle Tübingen
summary: Kunsthalle Tübingen will open Lars Eidinger. Present Perfect. In Dialogue with the Collection on October 10, bringing together the German actor and photographer’s images and videos with works by some of the most influential artists of the postwar period. Running through February 28, 2027, the exhibition will include more than 200 works and marks the first time Eidinger’s photography has been placed in direct dialogue with key holdings from Kunsthalle Tübingen’s collection. Eidinger has been taking photographs for more than three decades, first with a camera and later with his smartphone. His approach is instinctive and immediate. title: Pace presents group exhibition Exquisite Corpse curated by Loie Hollowell
summary: Pace presents Exquisite Corpse, an exhibition curated by Loie Hollowell (b. 1983, raised in Woodland, California) in response to her appreciation of the influential Austro-American artist Kiki Kogelnik (b. 1935, Graz, Austria; d. 1997, Vienna, Austria). In conversation with two of Hollowell’s contemporaries, Sascha Braunig (b. 1983, Qualicum Beach, Canada) and Veronika Pausova (b. 1987, Prague, Czech Republic), Hollowell discovered that Kogelnik’s work had equally impacted their own practices. This exhibition brings together works by all four cross-continental, multigenerational artists. “Exquisite corpse” is a collaborative parlor game invented by Surrealist artists in 1925. Players take turns either writing words or drawing sections of a body on a folded sheet of paper, hiding their contributions so the next person can see and respond to only the very end of the previous work. title: First New York Hans Arp exhibition in 15 years opens at Hauser & Wirth
summary: This Fall, Hauser & Wirth presents ‘Arp. Heads or Tails,’ the first New York exhibition in nearly fifteen years dedicated to the seminal German-French modernist. Organized by Curatorial Senior Director Alexis Lowry, in collaboration with the Stiftung Arp e.V., Berlin/Rolandswerth, this presentation takes Arp’s late Threshold sculptures as a point of departure, situating this pivotal but underexamined body of work within the trajectory of Arp’s long career of aesthetic and philosophical inquiry. The exhibition’s design takes inspiration from Arp’s studio in Locarno, Switzerland, and traces a line from his early cut-outs and reliefs to his mastery of form as a tool for reconfiguring and transforming our perception of space. ‘Heads or Tails’ presents key examples from the Threshold series alongside a selection

title: The Rollins Museum of Art announces National Advisory Task Force
summary: The Rollins Museum of Art at Rollins College announces the formation of a National Advisory Task Force as it prepares for the opening of its new, purpose-built facility in 2028, designed by Frederick Fisher and Partners. The Task Force will serve as advisors on the Museum’s opening and early programming. This group of colleagues from across the museum and arts fields was selected by Leslie Anne Anderson, RMA’s Bruce A. Beal Executive Director, for the relevance of their expertise to the strategic vision of the Museum. title: Oscar Peters builds monumental haunted house installation BARBARIAN at Monopole
summary: Dancing skeletons, gaping mouths, and a green maze with slowly moving walls. At Monopole, the artist Oscar Peters (1981) is building BARBARIAN, a monumental, haunted house inspired by fairground attractions, horror films, and amusement parks. Peters is fascinated by the never-ending human need to test the boundaries of fear. Wooden structures, theatrical effects, and strokes of paint are deliberately left exposed and turn the installation into a large-scale, handmade spectacle. Peters uses all the familiar ingredients of a classical haunted house – skulls, ghosts, a maze, and other archetypal tropes – to create a world where terror slowly makes way for questions about who we are and why we exist. In the end, the act of dwelling on such questions in a house with an exit that is difficult to find may well be the most terrifying thing of all. title: Margaret Rollins appointed Vice President, Development at George Eastman Museum
summary: The George Eastman Museum has appointed Margaret Rollins as Vice President, Development. She assumed this role on Monday, August 24. Rollins joins the Eastman Museum from the Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), where she served since 2021 as Senior Director for Advancement for the College of Science and the College of Liberal Arts. In that role, she led fundraising and advancement efforts for the colleges’ priorities and programs, including establishing national councils. Prior to joining RIT, Rollins held advancement positions at Nazareth College in Rochester, including Associate Director of Gift Planning and Assistant Director of Corporate, Foundation, and Government Relations. Rollins began her career working with several arts and cultural organizations, culminating in her position as Executive Director of the Smith Opera House in Geneva, New York. title: Tibor de Nagy Gallery presents Sarah McEneaney solo exhibition Porch Life
summary: Tibor de Nagy Gallery is presenting Sarah McEneaney: Porch Life, an exhibition of paintings from the last three years. The works in the current exhibition cover many of the areas McEneaney has explored over the last several decades. She continues her project of documenting her life and surroundings through self-portraits, interiors, cityscapes, and landscapes. The title Porch Life references both a literal porch and a stand-in for her studio, emphasizing the observational nature of this recent series—looking out and taking it in from an open-air studio. The artist is an avid traveler, and many paintings stem from a recent summer tour of Rhode Island and Maine. Another painting offers a porch view of her new home in New Jersey. Having attended many artist residencies throughout the world, she now maintains a second home and studio in rural South Jersey, which she describes as her “permanent residency.” The city of Philadelphia, where McEneaney has lived

title: Brussels exhibition highlights figures and oceanic landscapes by artist Kasper Sonne
summary: MARUANI MERCIER is presenting Kasper Sonne: People Are Strange, the second solo exhibition of the artist with the gallery, in Brussels. Elegant and upright, the figures in this new body of work appear at once in harmony with and in disassociation from the lucid planes of water and sky in the landscape. Looking away in quiet contemplation, the elongated human presence in each work projects an almost mythic quality, as if traversing the space in solitude that feels timeless rather than incidental. The paradox of iconic contemporary outfits in natural settings, together with the spectral light and the luminous palette in this new body of work projects a powerful sense of the instability of the human condition and questions the possibility of connection with another. As the artist notes, “For me, it's always this conflict – it's about displacement. I create these characters that have no obvious reason to be in these environments.”

title: Marcos Siqueira explores memory, nature, and earth pigments in new series at Mendes Wood DM
summary: To observe. This is the verb that comes to mind when I think of Marcos Siqueira’s paintings. Perhaps this is because the term recurs so often in our conversations. Siqueira frequently refers to his habit of sustained looking, of close attention, that he carries into his everyday activities. This daily exercise of slowing down and calibrating the senses has given him a discipline of attention to which almost nothing escapes: the geometric variation of the branches, leaves, and flowers of Brazil’s Serra do Cipó (some of which visit his paintings); the changing angles of incidence of light over the course of the day, with its refractions and reflections – among the trees, in the water, in the air, on natural objects; the great formations of shadows, born of the moving projections of one mountain over another. title: Tanya Bonakdar Gallery presents Sandra Vásquez de la Horra debut exhibition
summary: Tanya Bonakdar Gallery is presenting Reading the Waves, an exhibition of new work by Sandra Vásquez de la Horra. This is the artist’s first exhibition with the gallery. With drawing as the foundation of her artistic practice, Sandra Vásquez de la Horra creates a poetic visual universe that depicts the interconnectedness of the human body and the natural world. Taking inspiration from spiritual mythologies, folklore, religious iconographies, and Latin American popular imagery, she incorporates her anthropological interest in diverse healing practices and indigenous knowledge to promote a greater awareness of human interdependence with nature. title: Brazilian artist Anna Maria Maiolino debuts six-decade retrospective at Hauser & Wirth
summary: For more than six decades, Anna Maria Maiolino has pursued an expansive artistic practice shaped by her experiences of migration, motherhood and the complexities of daily life. Constantly reinventing her visual language, she has used drawing, photography, sculpture, performance and installation to plumb questions of corporeal existence, memory and the fundamental condition of being human. This September, Hauser & Wirth presents ‘ANNA—And the Infinite Line,’ an exhibition celebrating the acclaimed Brazilian artist’s enduring practice and the release of a documentary of the same title from The Forgotten Her Story. title: Becky Suss debuts new paintings exploring memory and night interiors at Jack Shainman
summary: Jack Shainman Gallery is presenting Night House, an exhibition of new work by Becky Suss that continues her exploration of interiority, domesticity and memory. Through paintings of imagined spaces and intimate vignettes, the exhibition marks a departure for Suss in her use of the darkness and quietude of the night as a lens through which to consider the emotional and psychological resonance of space. Suffused with the kind of specificity of detail that comes from the act of remembrance, Suss’ paintings reclaim the night not only as a time of reflection, but as one where perception deepens and self-knowledge can be pursued. title: Olney Gleason presents Sara Anstis solo exhibition Pastels in New York
summary: Olney Gleason is presenting a solo exhibition of new pastels on paper by London-based artist Sara Anstis (b. 1991), on view at 509 West 27th Street, New York, from September 10 through October 24, 2026. For Pastels, Anstis expands an allegorical universe informed by the visual languages of mythology, folklore, and art history. Realized at a small scale, the nearly thirty works on view encourage close looking while contrasting with the expanse of the gallery architecture. Anstis works in soft, delicate pastels, retaining an intimate sense of touch that charges her scenes with introspective intensity. In Pastels, Anstis draws from a deepened engagement with art history. Architecture and interiors assume a more pronounced role, contrasting with Anstis' archetypal landscapes, and her compositional structures recall sources ranging from medieval

title: Torkwase Dyson debuts new oceanic paintings inspired by deep-sea diving at Pace
summary: Pace is presenting Seeing in Blue, an exhibition of new paintings by Torkwase Dyson, at its 540 West 25th Street gallery from September 11 through October 24. Offering personal reflections on what the artist calls the “boundless state change of water,” the works on view strive toward the mindful presence needed to witness its beauty and devastation. Seeing in Blue spotlights a new series of paintings inspired by Dyson’s expeditions and sensory experiences as a deep-sea diver, exploring questions of distance, light, perception, symbiosis, and planetary transformation. The distilled works are informed by a culmination of haptic memories, diagrammatic drawings, engineering notes, photo journal entries, and process poems written by the artist during these explorations. title: Lava Thomas debuts large-scale portraits of post-Emancipation ancestors at Jessica Silverman
summary: Jessica Silverman is presenting “Lineage,” the gallery’s first exhibition with Lava Thomas, running through October 24, 2026. Known for her monumental portraits, Thomas’s newest body of work focuses on figures from her own ancestry in post-Emancipation Texas. On view will be eight large-scale graphite and Conté pencil drawings on paper alongside a series of hand-drawn reproductions of archival documentation. Following the gallery exhibition, works in the show will travel to Amon Carter Museum of American Art in Fort Worth, Texas for “Lava Thomas: In Our Own Regard,” curated by Michaela Haffner, Assistant Curator of Paintings, Sculpture, and Works on Paper opening November 7, 2026. title: Leaves: Eco-Anxiety explores ecological healing and remedies at ACE
summary: Presented at ACE 11 September to 5 December 2026, Leaves: Eco-Anxiety brings together artists Emiko Artemis, Alycia Bennett, Crista Bradshaw, Jingwei Bu, Bryce Cawte, Stephanie Doddridge, and Trudy Tandberg (1971–2026). The exhibition asks: amidst ecological polycrisis, what practical, cultural or mystical remedies are possible? Living with ecological crises has become part of everyday life. Climate change, habitat loss and environmental degradation bring with them anxiety and grief about what is happening to the natural world, and uncertainty about what comes next. Leaves: Eco-Anxiety considers not only the anxiety and grief these crises produce, but the possibilities for care, restoration, reflection and collective action. title: The Museum of Modern Art announces dates for its 2027 film festivals and annual series
summary: The Museum of Modern Art announces dates for its film festival lineup for 2027. To Save and Project returns for its 23rd year to present newly preserved and restored films from around the world, from January 7 to 31, 2027; Doc Fortnight will celebrate its 26th year highlighting a new crop of innovative nonfiction films, from February 25 to March 11, 2027; and the 56th edition of New Directors/New Films, co-presented by MoMA and Film at Lincoln Center, brings new work by emerging directors to the silver screen from April 7 to 18, 2027. Returning for its fifth year, Silent Movie Week, which brings seven silent-film restorations to MoMA over the course of one week, will run from July 28 to August 3, 2027. title: Dawn's Rock Garden opens at the George Eastman Museum following restoration
summary: The George Eastman Museum has completed the restoration and accessibility project for its historic Rock Garden. The garden has reopened as Dawn’s Rock Garden, named in recognition of Dr. Dawn F. Lipson and her support for the museum’s ongoing preservation projects. Gardens were important to George Eastman’s estate as a place to relax and entertain and as a backdrop for promotional photography to market Eastman Kodak products. Today, the gardens are a key part of the museum visitors’ experience and provide areas for quiet enjoyment by community members. Located near the University Avenue side of George Eastman’s former estate, the newly restored Dawn’s Rock Garden is now more visible and inviting since the removal of the fence along University Avenue in April. “We are deeply grateful to Dawn Lipson for her steadfast

title: Travesía Cuatro Madrid presents Vivian Suter solo exhibition Bajo el mango
summary: Travesía Cuatro is presenting Bajo el mango, an exhibition by artist Vivian Suter at Travesía Cuatro Madrid in collaboration with GAGA CDMX. "What lies beneath a mango tree? A rotting mango, fruits that turn black and burst with flies, ants, and bees, in a horrible and sweet swarm of life. And deeper down, the roots that drink secret waters, and pits that germinate, and pits that do not germinate and, as they decompose, return to the earth what the ancient roots that gave them life took from the earth. And even deeper down, the dead from whom dreams draw their nourishment.And deeper still, the mineral gods; and even deeper, the invisible and the unspeakable, which sometimes emanate to the surface like a breath. title: Kunsthalle Bern presents first Swiss solo exhibition by Saodat Ismailova
summary: Kunsthalle Bern is presenting the first solo exhibition in Switzerland of Uzbek artist and filmmaker Saodat Ismailova. Spanning both floors of the institution, Amanat—As We Sleep brings together seven large-scale video installations, centred around the newly commissioned film Amanat (2026). The exhibition marks the third and final chapter of a body of work that emerged from Ismailova’s sustained engagement with Arslanbob, an ancient walnut forest in Kyrgyzstan, following presentations at Swiss Institute in New York and LUMA Arles. Derived from the Arabic amānah, meaning “trust” or something entrusted to one’s care, amanat describes a relation to inheritance that resists possession. title: Gilbert & George present landmark survey at Palazzo della Ragione in Mantua
summary: Nearly two decades after their last major solo exhibition in Italy, Gilbert & George are back in the country with a focused presentation at the Sonnabend Collection Mantova, bringing together eight landmark works that span almost sixty years of the London-based duo’s career. Now on view at Palazzo della Ragione through April 5, 2027, the exhibition traces the artists’ enduring investigation of sex, politics, religion, urban identity and mortality, while also highlighting their long relationship with legendary dealer and collector Ileana Sonnabend. The eight works are being presented in Italy for the first time. The connection between Gilbert & George and the Sonnabend Gallery dates to 1971, when their celebrated performance The Singing Sculpture inaugurated Sonnabend’s New York space.
